**TypeScript** (**TS**) is a [high-level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-level_programming_language) [programming language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_language) that adds [static typing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Static_typing) with optional type [annotations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annotation#Software_and_engineering) to [JavaScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript). It is designed for developing large applications. It [transpiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source-to-source_compiler) to JavaScript.<sup>[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-6)</sup> It is developed by [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft) as [free and open-source software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_and_open-source_software) released under the [Apache License 2.0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_License_2.0).

TypeScript may be used to develop JavaScript applications for both [client-side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Client-side) and [server-side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Server-side) execution (as with [React.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/React.js), [Node.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node.js), [Deno](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deno_(software)>) or [Bun](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bun_(software)>)). Multiple options are available for transpiling. The default TypeScript Compiler can be used,<sup>[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-7)</sup> or the [Babel](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babel_(transcompiler)>) compiler can be invoked to convert TypeScript to JavaScript.

TypeScript supports definition files that can contain type information of existing JavaScript [libraries](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_(computing)>), much like [C++](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C++) [header files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Include_directive#Header_file) can describe the structure of existing [object files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object_file). This enables other programs to use the values defined in the files as if they were statically typed TypeScript entities. There are third-party header files for popular libraries such as [jQuery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JQuery), [MongoDB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MongoDB), and [D3.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D3.js). TypeScript headers for the [Node.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node.js) library modules are also available, allowing development of Node.js programs within TypeScript.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-8)

Before TypeScript 7.0, the TypeScript compiler was [written in TypeScript](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-hosting_(compilers)>) and [compiled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source-to-source_compiler) to JavaScript. In TypeScript 7.0, it was rewritten in [Go](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(programming_language)>).<sup>[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-9)</sup> It is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_License_2.0). [Anders Hejlsberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anders_Hejlsberg), lead architect of [C#](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_Sharp_(programming_language)>) and creator of [Delphi](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delphi_(software)>) and [Turbo Pascal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbo_Pascal), has worked on developing TypeScript.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-13)

TypeScript was released to the public in October 2012, with version 0.8, after two years of internal development at Microsoft.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-14)<sup>[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-15)</sup> Soon after the initial public release, [Miguel de Icaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_de_Icaza) praised the language, but criticized the lack of mature [integrated development environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_development_environment) (IDE) support apart from [Microsoft Visual Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Visual_Studio), which was unavailable then on [Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux) and [macOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS).[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-16)<sup>[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-17)</sup> As of April 2021 there is support in other IDEs and text editors, including [Emacs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emacs), [Vim](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vim_(text_editor)>), [WebStorm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JetBrains#WebStorm), [Atom](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(text_editor)>)<sup>[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-18)</sup> and Microsoft's own [Visual Studio Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Studio_Code).<sup>[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-19)</sup> TypeScript 0.9, released in 2013, added support for [generics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generic_programming).[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-20)

TypeScript 1.0 was released at Microsoft's [Build](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Build_(developer_conference)>) developer conference in 2014.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-21)[Visual Studio 2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Studio_2013) Update 2 provided built-in support for TypeScript.<sup>[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-22)</sup> Further improvement were made in July 2014, when the development team announced a new TypeScript compiler, asserted to have a five-fold performance increase. Simultaneously, the source code, which was initially hosted on [CodePlex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CodePlex), was moved to [GitHub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GitHub).[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-23)

On 22 September 2016, TypeScript 2.0 was released, introducing several features, including the ability for programmers to optionally enforce [null safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Null_safety).[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-24)

TypeScript 3.0 was released on 30 July 2018,<sup>[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-25)</sup> bringing many language additions like tuples in rest parameters and spread expressions, rest parameters with tuple types, generic rest parameters and so on.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-26)

TypeScript 4.0 was released on 20 August 2020.<sup>[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-27)</sup> While 4.0 did not introduce any breaking changes, it added language features such as Custom [JSX](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSX_(JavaScript)>) Factories and Variadic Tuple Types.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-27)

TypeScript 5.0 was released on 16 March 2023 and included support for decorators.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-28)

On March 11, 2025, Anders Hejlsberg announced on the TypeScript blog that the team is working on a [Go](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(programming_language)>) port of the TypeScript compiler to be released as TypeScript version 7.0 later this year. It is expected to feature a 10x [speedup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedup).[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-29)

On December 2nd, 2025, Daniel Rosenwasser announced on the blog that TypeScript 6.0 will be the last release written in TypeScript itself, and TypeScript 7.0 will be the first Go-based release.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-30)

TypeScript originated from the shortcomings of JavaScript for developing large-scale applications both at Microsoft and among their external customers.<sup>[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-31)</sup> Challenges with dealing with complex JavaScript code led to demand for custom tooling to ease developing of components in the language.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-32)

Developers sought a solution that would not break compatibility with the [ECMAScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECMAScript) (ES) standard and its ecosystem, so a [compiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler) was developed to transform a superset of JavaScript with type annotations and classes (TypeScript files) back into vanilla ECMAScript 5 code. TypeScript classes were based on the then-proposed ECMAScript 6 class specification to make writing [prototypal inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prototype-based_programming) less verbose and error-prone, and type annotations enabled [IntelliSense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_completion) and improved tooling.

TypeScript adds the following syntax extensions to JavaScript:

- [Type signatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_signature) (annotations) and [compile-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compile-time) [type checking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_checking)
- [Type inference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_inference)
- [Interfaces](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interface_(object-oriented_programming)>)
- [Enumerated types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enumerated_type)
- [Generics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generic_programming)
- [Namespaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namespace)
- [Tuples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuple)

Syntactically, TypeScript is very similar to [JScript .NET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JScript_.NET), another Microsoft implementation of the ECMA-262 language standard that added support for static typing and classical object-oriented language features such as classes, inheritance, interfaces, and namespaces. Other inspirations include [Java](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_(programming_language)>) and [C#](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_Sharp_(programming_language)>).

As TypeScript is simply a superset of JavaScript, existing JavaScript can be adapted to TypeScript while TypeScript can seamlessly integrate JavaScript. The compiler can target all ECMAScript versions 5 and above, transpiling modern features like classes and arrow functions to their older counterparts.

With TypeScript, it is possible to use existing JavaScript code, incorporate popular JavaScript libraries, and call TypeScript-generated code from other JavaScript.<sup>[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-typescript-home-page-33)</sup> Type declarations for these libraries are usually provided with the source code but can be declared or installed separately if needed.

Prior to version 7, the TypeScript compiler, named `tsc`, was [written in TypeScript](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-hosting_(compilers)>) and compiled into regular JavaScript, allowing it to run in any JavaScript engine (e.g. a browser) or as a [Node.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node.js) package. Beginning with TypeScript 7.0, released on 8 July 2026, the compiler and language service were rewritten in [Go](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(programming_language)>) as a native binary, which Microsoft reported delivers full-build speedups typically between 8 and 12 times over the JavaScript-based TypeScript 6.0 compiler; for example, type-checking the Visual Studio Code codebase fell from 125.7 seconds to 10.6 seconds under default settings.<sup>[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-infoq70-34)</sup> The native port began as an experimental preview distributed via the `@typescript/native-preview` npm package starting in 2025, which had accumulated more than 8.5 million weekly downloads before being merged into the standard `typescript` package for the 7.0 release.<sup>[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-infoq70-34)</sup> TypeScript 7.0 shipped without a stable programmatic compiler API, which Microsoft said would be introduced in a subsequent 7.1 release; in the interim, tooling that depends on the compiler's API, such as certain features of Vue, Angular, and Svelte, required continued use of the JavaScript-based compiler.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-infoq70-34)

The compiler can *target* a given edition of ECMAScript (such as [ECMAScript 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECMAScript_version_history) for legacy browser compatibility), but by default compiles for the latest standards.

In 2026, [Vercel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vercel) released scriptc, an open-source compiler that compiles TypeScript and [JavaScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript) programs into self-contained native executables without requiring [Node.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node.js), [V8](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V8_(JavaScript_engine)>), or another JavaScript engine in the resulting binary.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-35)

Using [plug-ins](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plug-in_(computing)>), TypeScript can be integrated with [build automation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Build_automation) tools, including Grunt (grunt-ts<sup>[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-41)</sup>), [Apache Maven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_Maven) (TypeScript Maven Plugin<sup>[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-42)</sup>), Gulp (gulp-typescript<sup>[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-43)</sup>) and [Gradle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradle) (TypeScript Gradle Plugin<sup>[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-44)</sup>).
